Any features in this subclass that use a Psionic Energy Die use only the dice from this subclass. Some of your powers expend a Psionic Energy Die, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your Psionic Energy Dice are all expended.

You regain one of your expended Psionic Energy Dice when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB], and you regain all of them when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Psi-Bolstered Knack. If you fail an ability check using a skill or tool with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended only if the roll then succeeds.

Psychic Whispers. You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, choose one or more creatures you can see, up to a number of creatures equal to your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus], and then roll one Psionic Energy Die. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, the chosen creatures can speak telepathically with you, and you can speak telepathically with them. To send or receive a message (no action required), you and the other creature must be within 1 mile of each other. A creature can end the telepathic connection at any time (no action required).

The first time you use this power after each @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you don't expend the Psionic Energy Die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.

Level 3: Psychic Blades

You can manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action or make an @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB], you can manifest a @item[Psychic Blade|XPHB] in your free hand and make the attack with that blade. The magic blade has the following traits:

Psychic Blade
[+]
Loading "@item[Psychic Blade|XPHB]"...

The blade vanishes immediately after it hits or misses its target, and it leaves no mark if it deals damage.

After you attack with the blade on your turn, you can make a melee or ranged attack with a second psychic blade as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] on the same turn if your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is [[/damage 1d4]] instead of [[/damage 1d6]].

Level 9: Soul Blades

You can now use the following powers with your Psychic Blades.

Homing Strikes. If you make an attack roll with your @item[Psychic Blade|XPHB] and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. If this causes the attack to hit, the die is expended.

Psychic Teleportation. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you manifest a @item[Psychic Blade|XPHB], expend one Psionic Energy Die and roll it, and throw the blade at an unoccupied space you can see up to a number of feet away equal to 10 times the number rolled. You then teleport to that space, and the blade vanishes.

Level 13: Psychic Veil

You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you gain the &Reference[condition=Invisible] condition for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a saving throw.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] unless you expend a Psionic Energy Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

Level 17: Rend Mind

You can sweep your Psychic Blades through a creature's mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus]). If the save fails, the target has the &Reference[condition=Stunned] condition for 1 minute. The &Reference[condition=Stunned] target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] unless you expend three Psionic Energy Dice (no action required) to restore your use of it.

You gain @variantrule[Expertise|XPHB] in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. &Reference[skill=SleightofHand]{Sleight of Hand} and &Reference[skill=Stealth] are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Rogue level 6, you gain @variantrule[Expertise|XPHB] in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra [[/damage 1d6]] damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, and you don't have @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on the attack roll.

The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in chapter 2.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as @item[Dagger|XPHB|Daggers] and @item[Shortbow|XPHB|Shortbows].

Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of @item[Scimitar|XPHB|Scimitars] and @item[Shortsword|XPHB|Shortswords].

Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB]: @action[Dash|XPHB], @action[Disengage|XPHB], or @action[Hide|XPHB].

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you give yourself @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] is 0 until the end of the current turn.

General Feat (Prerequisite: Proficiency with @item[whip|PHB] or @item[tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting])

Your skill with whips and tetherhooks allows you to manipulate items at a distance.

  • Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When you hit a creature with an attack using a @item[tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting] or @item[whip|PHB], you can use a bonus action to attempt to disarm the creature of a shield, or of one item it is holding. Make a Strength or Dexterity check (your choice) contested by the target's Strength check. If you succeed, the item is dropped on the ground midway between you and the creature.
  • You can use your @item[whip|PHB] or @item[tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting] to grab items weighing less than 1 lb within the reach of your weapon, pulling them back to your person.

Mastery: Nick. When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the @action[Attack|XPHB] action instead of as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB]. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Mastery: Vex. If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

Arrows are used with a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

Arrows are typically stored in a @item[Quiver|XPHB] (bought separately).
A Quiver holds up to 20 Arrows.

• Ability: Dexterity

  • Utilize: Pick a lock (DC 15), or disarm a trap (DC 15)
A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

As a @action[Utilize|XPHB] action, you can spill Ball Bearings from their pouch. They spread to cover a level, 10-foot-square area within 10 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=10]] saving throw or have the &Reference[condition=Prone] condition. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Ball Bearings.
When rung as a @action[Utilize|XPHB] action, a Bell produces a sound that can be heard up to 60 feet away.
For 1 hour, a lit Candle sheds @variantrule[Bright Light|XPHB] in a 5-foot radius and @variantrule[Dim Light|XPHB] for an additional 5 feet.
Using a Crowbar gives you @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Strength checks where the Crowbar's leverage can be applied.

A Hooded Lantern burns Oil as fuel to cast @variantrule[Bright Light|XPHB] in a 30-foot radius and @variantrule[Dim Light|XPHB] for an additional 30 feet. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can lower the hood, reducing the light to @variantrule[Dim Light|XPHB] in a 5-foot radius, or raise it again.

You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus]) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra 5 Fire damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the @action[Utilize|XPHB] action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn't need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a @action[Utilize|XPHB] action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.
Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See "@hazard[Malnutrition|XPHB]" for the risks of not eating.

As a @action[Utilize|XPHB] action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=10]] (&Reference[skill=SleightofHand]{Sleight of Hand}) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful [[/save ability=str dc=20]] (&Reference[skill=Athletics]) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the &Reference[condition=Grappled], &Reference[condition=Incapacitated], or &Reference[condition=Restrained] condition. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the &Reference[condition=Restrained] condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful [[/save ability=dex dc=15]] (&Reference[skill=Acrobatics]) check as an action.

A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a @item[Candle|XPHB], @item[Lamp|XPHB], @item[Hooded Lantern|XPHB|Lantern], or @item[Torch|XPHB]—or anything else with exposed fuel—takes a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB]. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.
A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk dehydration.

Elscieth is a spellcaster, her spellcasting ability is Charisma.
Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

You can see and hear a creature you choose that is on the same plane of existence as you. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw, which is modified (see the tables below) by how well you know the target and the sort of physical connection you have to it. The target doesn't know what it is making the save against, only that it feels uneasy.

Your Knowledge of the Target Is …Save Modifier
Secondhand (heard of the target)+5
Firsthand (met the target)+0
Extensive (know the target well)−5
You Have the Target's …Save Modifier
Picture or other likeness−2
Garment or other possession−4
Body part, lock of hair, or bit of nail−10

On a successful save, the target isn't affected, and you can't use this spell on it again for 24 hours.

On a failed save, the spell creates an Invisible, intangible sensor within 10 feet of the target. You can see and hear through the sensor as if you were there. The sensor moves with the target, remaining within 10 feet of it for the duration. If something can see the sensor, it appears as a luminous orb about the size of your fist.

Instead of targeting a creature, you can target a location you have seen. When you do so, the sensor appears at that location and doesn't move.

A beam of crackling energy streaks toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 force damage.

The spell creates more than one beam when you reach higher levels: two beams at 5th level, three beams at 11th level, and four beams at 17th level. You can direct the beams at the same target or at different ones. Make a separate attack roll for each beam.

You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

You teleport yourself from your current location to any other spot within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction, such as "200 feet straight downward" or "upward to the northwest at a 45-degree angle, 300 feet."

You can bring along objects as long as their weight doesn't exceed what you can carry. You can also bring one willing creature of your size or smaller who is carrying gear up to its carrying capacity. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you cast this spell.

If you would arrive in a place already occupied by an object or a creature, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 force damage, and the spell fails to teleport you.

You weave a distracting string of words, causing creatures of your choice that you can see within range and that can hear you to make a Wisdom saving throw. Any creature that can't be Charmed succeeds on this saving throw automatically, and if you or your companions are fighting a creature, it has advantage on the save. On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to perceive any creature other than you until the spell ends or until the target can no longer hear you. The spell ends if you are Incapacitated or can no longer speak.
This spell allows you to move at an incredible pace. When you cast this spell, and then as a bonus action on each of your turns until the spell ends, you can take the Dash action.
A creature you touch has the Invisible condition until the spell ends.

Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or 8 hours (Enrichment)

This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting time you use determines whether the spell has the Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.

Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through that area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested. They can benefit from only one Plant Growth per year.

Eight rays of light flash from you in a 60-foot Cone. Each creature in the Cone makes a Dexterity saving throw. For each target, roll 1d8 to determine which color ray affects it, consulting the Prismatic Rays table.

If it successfully saves three times, the condition ends. If it fails three times, it has the &Reference[Petrified] condition until it is freed by an effect like the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplGreaterRes]{Greater Restoration} spell. The successes and failures needn’t be consecutive; keep track of both until the target collects three of a kind.

effects.name: Teleporting (Violet)
effects.description: The target has the &Reference[Blinded apply=false] condition and makes a [[/save ability=wis format=long]] at the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the condition ends. On a failed save, the condition ends, and the creature teleports to another plane of existence (DM’s choice).

description.value: Elscieth transforms into the dragon form of Sylvaria. Unlike other polymorphs, she does not gain a new hit point pool but rather uses the hit points of @UUID[Actor.h0g8nVSDHjwhvoKB]{Sylvaria}.

A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

When you cast the spell, you can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

As a Magic action on your later turns, you can control the hand thus again. As part of that action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

Objects in a 20-foot Cube within range are outlined in blue, green, or violet light (your choice). Each creature in the Cube is also outlined if it fails a Dexterity saving throw. For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed &Reference[dimlight] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

Attack rolls against an affected creature or object have Advantage if the attacker can see it.

Choose one creature or nonmagical object that you can see within range. You transform the creature into a different creature, the creature into a nonmagical object, or the object into a creature (the object must be neither worn nor carried by another creature). The transformation lasts for the duration, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. If you concentrate on this spell for the full Duration, the transformation lasts until it is dispelled.

This spell has no effect on a target with 0 Hit Points. An unwilling creature can make a Wisdom saving throw, and if it succeeds, it isn't affected by this spell.

Creature into Creature. If you turn a creature into another kind of creature, the new form can be any kind you choose whose challenge rating is equal to or less than the target's (or its level, if the target doesn't have a Challenge rating). The target's game statistics, including mental Ability Scores, are replaced by the statistics of the new form. It retains its Alignment and personality.

The target assumes the hit points of its new form, and when it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the number of Hit Points it had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hit points, it isn't knocked Unconscious.

The creature is limited in the Actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can't speak, cast Spells, or take any other action that requires hands or speech, unless its new form is capable of such Actions.

The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its Equipment.

Object into Creature. You can turn an object into any kind of creature, as long as the creature's size is no larger than the object's size and the creature's Challenge rating is 9 or lower. The creature is friendly to you and your companions. It acts on each of your turns. You decide what action it takes and how it moves. The DM has the creature's Statistics and resolves all of its Actions and Movement.

If the spell becomes permanent, you no longer control the creature. It might remain friendly to you, depending on how you have treated it.

Creature into Object. If you turn a creature into an object, it transforms along with whatever it is wearing and carrying into that form. The creature's statistics become those of the object, and the creature has no memory of time spent in this form, after the spell ends and it returns to its normal form.

Xanaris, Eyes that Bite p262

“Xanaris is the biggest and most diabolical of the eyes that bite. Colloquially known as the Mage-Eater or the Arcane Maw, in our last encounter he said he would eat me last so I could watch every ounce of magic fade from the world before I perish. That battle served as a grim reminder of the importance of diversity in one's adventuring companions. Without the quick blade-work of Ava Sonos, I would never have penned this tome, and such a tragic future is best left uncontemplated. At heart, Xanaris is a @creature[yeti|MM], a creature of the mountains that is afraid of fire. The void twisted and magnified his hatred, and he works to return the world to a magic-less state. A future I obviously prefer to avoid.”

— Talien Vos Karven

Classification: Brute

Favors: Barbarians, Fear (Protection from), Mobility (high), Monks, Rogues

Foils: Sorcerers, Spells, Warlocks, Weapons (Magical), Wizards

Humanoids, giants, and others of similar ilk touched by the void swell with physical strength, becoming hulking brutes that devour magic (and magic-users) with abandon. Whatever form these poor creatures once held is replaced with a convulsing mass of tentacled shadows. Their eyes fill with a bleak redness that saps the life from all who stare into them, and their incisors are lined with runes that drain the magic from their victims. They are without compassion, filled with the deepest hunger for arcana in all its forms.

“Wizard's woe, wizard's woe

Teeth so long and twin red glow

Get in bed and douse the light

Sunset calls the eyes that bite!”

— Unattributed nursery rhyme

Lore

A character can learn the following information about an eyes that bite with an Intelligence (&Reference[skill=Arcana]), Intelligence (&Reference[skill=Nature]), or Intelligence (&Reference[skill=Religion]) ability check.

Eyes that Bite Lore
DCInformation
17There are rumors of massive shadowy creatures that suck the magic from other creatures the way a @creature[vampire|MM] sucks blood. Dubbed the "eyes that bite" by the few survivors, these twisted echoes were once large and powerful creatures before direct contact with the void.
22Eyes that bire are brutal voidborn of prodigious strength. They project an aura of antimagic, and their bites drain the magical energy out of a spellcaster, healing the eyes that bite in the process. Though not especially quick, the void energy flowing through them allows them to fly.
27While devastating to spellcasters, eyes that bite have no special abilities to suppress or protect themselves from nonmagical items. Nonmagical hindrances such as steel nets and traps can buy time but given the great strength of the eyes that bite, such reprieves are temporary.

Tactics

Eyes that bite are patient hunters that become utterly reckless when they leap into battle. They fixate on a spellcaster and stalk it until they get close enough to attack, and they will wait for a short time to try to get their prey alone. If that isn't an option, they attack anyway. An eyes that bite starts out using Void Breath on the spellcaster's allies, then it rushes into melee range and begins biting the spellcaster. It focuses on its target until it has drained every ounce of the caster's magical energy, the target is dead, or both.

Don't forget about its Gaze into the Void trait—the party should be constantly debating whether to avert their eyes or take the risk of nearly lethal damage. When using Null Zone, focus on any effect that is preventing the eyes that bite from moving or taking actions. Damaging spells are less important. Use Void Breath every time it recharges, primarily to split the party and block line of sight so it becomes more difficult for them to help each other.

Easier Tactics - Spread out Bite attacks between multiple targets, and spend some time attacking characters who aren't spellcasters. You can also have the eyes that bite retreat when reduced to fewer than half its hit point maximum, giving the party time to catch their breath and heal before chasing it down.

Harder Tactics - Use Void Breath on the spellcaster target and run the eyes that bite into melee combat with the caster to finish the job. The eyes that bite won't take damage from its own Void Breath cloud, and its &Reference[rule=truesight] allows it to see clearly in the darkness. Unless the party has their own means of seeing through the darkness, the spellcaster inside is going to be dead in short order. Remember that most teleportation effects like @spell[misty step] specify "a location you can see," and a caster surrounded by magical darkness can see little.

Plot Hooks

Predator. An eyes that bite picks a spellcaster in the party as its next target. It keeps a safe distance, waiting for the character to become separated from the party before striking. The creature wants to keep the PC alive as an inexhaustible supply of magical energy.

Grisly Fate. A giant the party knows is corrupted by the void, perhaps by accident, or perhaps in a valiant act of self-sacrifice. It demands the party kill it before it's too late. Should the party wait too long before acting, the giant will transform into an eyes that bite.

Trouble At School. A pair of eyes that bite takes up residence in the forest outside a wizarding school or bardic college, and students are disappearing. Then the teachers tsart to vanish too. Soon the school will be an empty shell.

Xanaris, The Mage-Eater p264

When he was a mere @creature[yeti|MM], Xanaris lived in an uneasy balance with the mountain folk. He would eat those who wandered too far afield, and they would chase him away with spears and torches when he came too close to the vilalge. War was not uncommon in those times, and during a particularly violent conflict, Xanaris stole into the closest village to steal an easy meal in the confusion. But the humans had discovered a new kind of fire. A cadre of mages sent a fusillade of fire and shadow, light and lightning, churning the snow and bodies into bloody mush. Xanaris, his body battered, and bones broken, crawled from the wreckage, sheer anger holding him conscious.

In the wake of this brutality, the void stretched its inky tendrils out of the embers and took hold of the @creature[yeti|MM]. Already large for his kind, the void coursed through him, turning his shaggy fur pitch black, his eyes red, and cursing him with a bottomless hunger. Xanaris hunted down and slew every mage on the mountain, devouring their essence in a fruitless attempt to slake the unslakable. Xanaris then traveled far from the mountain on which he once lived, traversing much of the material plane and other realms pretending to be no more than a simple-minded beast.

Treasure

By their very nature, voidborn leave little behind when they are slain. Their bodies collapse into nothingness, fading into the void that gave them life. The death of a voidborn—and the resulting collapse in the void—can sometimes cause an upswelling of magic as the weave rushes in, and in these cases, a @item[solstice star|TPK] is formed. This tiny sphere offers protections against magic and from the energies of the void, and they are held in high regard by spellcasters and those who hunt voidborn. Such individuals would pay 15,000 gp for a @item[solstice star|TPK].

Ecology

Eyes that bite spend the entirety of their existence hunting spellcasters—they have no other purpose. Gifted with an instinctual understanding of magic, eyes that bite are able to circumvent most magical defenses undetected. These voidborn only travel under the cover of darkness and will cross great distances in search of new prey. Eyes that bite will take great care to avoid being spotted by anyone, as even a rumor of its presence can send the most laid-back bard running to the hills. While they have no interest in nonmagical creatures, eyes that bite will not tolerate any threat to its existence, attacking anything that threatens its lair. However, they will cooperate with anything that can provide a hearty meal of powerful magic. More than a few evil spellcasters have been brought down by a good aligned foe willing to make a deal with the devil.

Voidborn

For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction, and magic is no different. As civilization flourishes and magic becomes commonplace, the price of its use remains largely unknown and unseen. Every work of magic—minor or mighty, arcane or divine—leaves behind a void. At first a mere curiosity, millennia of abundant magic use has strengthened it, matured it, and given it a mind all its own. The void, known most commonly as "antimagic," is the check and balance, and it is eager to set the world right. Pulsing like a dark heart, the void seeks to eat magic, birthing and shaping creations to feed its dark hunger.

Voidborn are the answer to magical creatures and beings, even though many of them were at one time magical themselves. They are typically created in the aftermath of great magical works, whether it be the casting of a @spell[wish] spell, the creation of a magical artifact, or a world-ending battle between spellcasters. More than a few archmages have been consumed by a survivor of their most powerful spells, the creature endowed with mysterious powers from an unknown source.

Each voidborn is radically different from all others. Their origins are bizarre, but they are bound together by the void's warping hunger. The transformation process is trying, and the strain is well beyond what most can bear. When the transformation ends, a voidborn's senses are honed to razor sharpness, and the unending hunger birthed within them spurs them on toward the nearest source of magic.

Talien's Notes p258

No subject is of greater interest to the arcane community than the void. Indeed, it serves as an object of common study for those who channel magic of the gods or of nature, or those who are even remotely invested in the long-term survival of this world. I will summarize. All magic, whatever the source, draws power from the weave. It leaves behind a gap, a void, which diminishes as the weave naturally restores itself. In the past, this was hardly a matter of concern, for few could use enough magic to create more than a pinprick void in the weave. But in this age of arcane abundance, our over-reliance of spells is creating something dangerous—void pockets that do not shrink. Instead, they grow. They hunger. They think and scheme. These creatures are called the voidborn. There is no good outcome here, no place for them in the natural cycle. They must be destroyed.

Void Influence

The void leaves no being untouched. Whether merely grazed by its shadow or fully bathed in its energy, if creatures walk away from a brush with the void, they are changed by the experience. Thankfully the void's presence is rare, typically appearing in areas that have been subjected to considerable magical damage. Characters that are directly exposed to such areas or to voidborn creatures can become affected by the latent energy, gaining a void influence. When choosing a void influence, select deliberately from the options in the void influence table, roll a [[/r d8]] to determine the effect, or feel free to come up with your own. At your discretion, these changes last until removed by @spell[greater restoration] or more powerful magic, or they may be permanent.

Void Influence
[[/r d8]]Effect
1You become unable to sleep peacefully, wracked with nightmares about being trapped in a slug's body as salt is poured upon you by laughing, faceless figures.
2Toadstools randomly grow from your skin and hair, often in bright, vibrant colors. Trying to remove them is painful, and they always grow back within 24 hours.
3You grow older or younger by [[/r 1d12]] years, at the DM's discretion.
4You always perceive whispers at the edge of your hearing but are unable to make out what is being said. No one else can hear the whispers, and people look at you askance when you bring them up.
5You can see a ghostly afterimage of yourself, and others can see it too. It doesn't always appear, and it doesn't always match what you do exactly. Sometimes it fails where you succeed, and other times it succeeds where you fail.
6You gain an unquenchable thirst for drugs and alcohol, desperate to forget the things you have seen.
7Animals dislike you; dogs bark and cats hiss when you pass by. They smell the otherworldly stench upon you.
8Eyes randomly appear on your skin but switch places from day to day. You can see out of them.

Voidtouched Template p259

Those who come into prolonged contact with the void are changed irrevocably. Such creatures are voidtouched, altered into strange new forms and bound to the whims of the voidborn. The following template can be applied to any creature, for the void does not discriminate. It should not be applied to characters—characters with this much exposure to the void are no longer under the players' control and instead become creatures controlled by the DM.

Type. The creature's type changes to aberration.

Damage Resistances. The creature gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from magic weapons.

Condition Immunities. The creature gains immunity to the &Reference[condition=charmed] and &Reference[condition=frightened] conditions.

Challenge. The creature's Challenge Rating increases by 3.

Traits. The creature gains the following traits:

  • Draining Aura. At the start of each of the voidtouched creature's turns, creatures within 10 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + the voidtouched creature's proficiency bonus + its Wisdom modifier) or lose 6 ([[/r 1d12]]) hit points, and have their hit point maximum is reduced to their current hit points. This effect can only be removed by @spell[greater restoration] or similar healing magic. If a creature's hit point maximum would be reduced to 0 by this feature, it is reduced to 1 instead.

  • Void Resilience. The voidtouched has resistance to all damage from spells and has advantage on saving throws against spells. If the voidtouched succeeds on a saving throw against a spell and suffers an effect on the success, it instead suffers no effect.

Actions. The creature gains the following actions.

  • Consume Arcane (Recharge [[/r 1d6]]{5–6}). The voidtouched chooses up to six creatures it can see within 120 feet and attempts to siphon magic from them. Targets must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + the voidtouched creature's proficiency bonus + its Wisdom modifier) or expend two spell slots of their choice. The voidtouched regains 10 hit points per level of each spell slot lost, and the target takes 7 ([[/r 2d6]]) psychic damage per level of each spell slot lost.

  • Strength of the Void. A voidtouched creature's attacks no longer cause damage; instead, the target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage the attack would have dealt.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from magic weapons

description.value: The eyes that bite makes two Bite attacks. The eyes that bite can replace one of its Bite attacks with Void Breath.

Melee Weapon Attack: [[/r 1d20+14]]{+14} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: The target loses 30 ([[/r 5d8 + 8]]) hit points must expend one unexpended spell slot of its choice. The eyes that bite regains 7 ([[/r 2d6]]) hit points per level of the spell slot expended.

The eyes that bite exhales void energy in a 15-foot-wide, 30-foot-long line. Each creature in that area must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=20]] saving throw or lose 52 ([[/r 8d12]]) hit points, or half as much on a success.

Additionally, the affected area becomes filled with magical darkness for 1 minute. Sound cannot be produced in the area, and when an enemy creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn within the area, it must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=20]] saving throw or lose 52 ([[/r 8d12]]) hit points, or half as much on a success.

At the start of each of its turns, creatures within 30 feet of the eyes that bite must succeed on a [[/save ability=wis dc=20]] saving throw or lose 19 ([[/r 3d12]]) hit points and have their hit point maximum reduced to their current hit points. This effect can only be removed by @spell[greater restoration] or similar healing magic. If a creature's hit point maximum would be reduced to 0 by this feature, it is reduced to 1 instead.

When a creature that can see the eyes that bite starts its turn within 30 feet of it, the eyes that bite can force it to attempt a [[/save ability=con dc=20]] saving throw if the eyes that bite isn't &Reference[condition=incapacitated] and can see the creature. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is reduced to 0 hit points. Otherwise, the creature takes 21 ([[/damage 6d6 type=psychic]]) damage on a failure, or half a s much on a success. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its gaze to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If a creature does so, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against the eyes that bite until the start of its next turn. If the creature looks at the eyes that bite in the meantime, it must immediately attempt the saving throw.

The eyes that bite has advantage on Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) ability checks that rely on smell.

Additionally, the eyes that bite can smell spells and magical effects up to 1 mile away and can track a creature by scent up to one hour after the creature casts a spell.

The eyes that bite cannot be targeted by any divination magic or through magical scrying sensors. Additionally, the eyes that bite is &Reference[condition=invisible] to creatures that have one or more unexpended spell slots.

The eyes that bite has resistance to all damage from spells and advantage on saving throws to resist spells. If the eyes that bite succeeds on a saving throw against a spell and suffers an effect on the success, it instead suffers no effect.

As a reaction when a creature the eyes that bite can see casts a spell, it can attempt to interrupt the casting. The caster must immediately expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher as part of casting the spell, or the spell fails.

biography.value:
Gzemnid is a beholder god of deception, gases, and obscurement.

The realm of the beholder deity Gzemnid lies beneath the Outlands. Most entrances into these mysterious, gas-filled caverns are found near chaotically aligned gate-towns—like Bedlam, Sylvania, or Xaos—but Gzemnid's Realm is elusive, even by the mutable standards of the Outlands.

description.value: The eyestalk attacks with its bite and uses Eradication Gaze.

Melee Weapon Attack: [[/r 1d20+14]]{+14} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 ([[/damage 3d8 + 9 type=piercing]]) damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=19]] saving throw or be swallowed by the eyestalk. A swallowed creature is &Reference[condition=blinded] and &Reference[condition=restrained], it has &Reference[rule=totalcover]{total cover} against attacks and other effects outside the eyestalk, and it takes 21 ([[/damage 6d6 type=acid]]) damage at the start of each of the eyestalk's turns.

If the eyestalk takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the eyestalk must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=21]] saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall &Reference[condition=prone] in a space within 10 feet of the eyestalk. If the eyestalk dies, a swallowed creature is no longer &Reference[condition=restrained] by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting &Reference[condition=prone].

The eyestalk creates an area of magical devastation in a 150-foot cone. Any creature in that area must succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=16]] saving throw or take 55 ([[/damage 10d10 type=necrotic]]) damage. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 hit points, its body becomes a pile of fine violet dust.
The eyestalk can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

biography.value:
Fawful — The Assistant Who Became the Architect

Fawful is the most dangerous individual currently operating in the Mushroom Kingdom's sphere of influence who is not a god, a dimensional anomaly, or a force of nature. He is a small Beanish man with enormous glasses, speech patterns that weaponize grammar into incomprehensibility, and a mind that processes strategic complexity the way other minds process breathing—automatically, constantly, without conscious effort, producing results that make brilliant analysts feel stupid and careful planners feel careless.

He started as an assistant. This is the detail that every analyst who studies Fawful returns to with mounting horror, because the things Fawful has accomplished since ceasing to be someone else's assistant suggest capabilities that were always present but previously constrained by service to a lesser intellect. Cackletta, the witch he served during the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis of 1012 BF, was powerful. Fawful was something else entirely. Cackletta wanted a voice. Fawful wanted everything.

When Mario and Luigi defeated Cackletta in the Beanbean Kingdom, Fawful escaped. He disappeared from records for twenty-eight years. Official histories assumed he was dead, irrelevant, a footnote in a crisis that had been resolved. This assumption was incorrect in ways that are now horrifyingly apparent.

During those twenty-eight years, Fawful was building. Not visibly—there were no armies, no territories, no declarations of intent. He was building QUIETLY, assembling a network of alliances, resources, and capabilities that nobody detected until it was too late to prevent. He built relationships with dragons—not one dragon, not two, but five confirmed alliances with creatures whose individual power exceeds conventional military formations. He established himself in Mushroom Kingdom territory by taking advantage of the civil war's chaos, occupying positions that nobody else wanted because nobody else saw their strategic value. He planted agents in every faction, cultivated intelligence sources that span the political spectrum, and developed technology that combines Beanish ingenuity with sources of power that legitimate engineers won't touch.

By the time the current crisis began, Fawful had been the most powerful non-state actor in the region for at least a decade, and nobody knew. He revealed himself on Highsun 10, 1040 BF, by hosting a victory gala—a social event attended by scouts from multiple factions, during which Fawful casually announced his dragon alliances and demonstrated a level of organizational capability that intelligence services across the kingdom had completely failed to detect. The gala served multiple purposes: it established Fawful as a power to be negotiated with rather than dismissed; it provided cover for intelligence operations by Embercap and Mistveil (during which Chief Thornpaw's revelation about Peach's secret hatch was extracted); and it announced to everyone paying attention that the civil war's factional landscape had just acquired a new, major player who had been preparing for this moment for nearly three decades.

Fawful currently controls Peach's Castle—the symbolic and strategic heart of the Mushroom Kingdom, occupied through mechanisms that suggest either overwhelming force or infiltration so complete that resistance was irrelevant by the time his occupation became visible. His garrison is estimated at over five hundred personnel, supplemented by mechanical constructs of his own design, supported by dragon allies whose individual combat capability exceeds what most military formations can counter. Operation HOMECOMING—Mistveil's infiltration to locate the secret hatch—operates inside this fortress, with four operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff, surrounded by forces that could destroy them instantly if their cover was compromised.

Understanding Fawful requires understanding that his apparent chaos is performance. The speech patterns—"I HAVE FURY!" and the elaborate food metaphors and the grammar that seems to have been assembled by someone who learned language from a malfunctioning dictionary—are deliberate. They make him seem unhinged. They make opponents underestimate his intelligence. They create cognitive dissonance between what Fawful says and what Fawful does, forcing anyone interacting with him to choose between taking his words seriously (which makes them seem foolish when the words are nonsensical) and dismissing his words (which makes them miss genuine intelligence buried in the metaphors).

Fawful is not unhinged. Fawful is the most rationally calculating entity in the current crisis who also happens to express himself like a caffeinated thesaurus having a breakdown. The calculations are perfect. The expression is theater. And the theater serves the calculations, because nobody prepares adequate defenses against someone they've decided is a clown.

His grudge against the Mario Brothers—specifically against Luigi, "the green mustache"—has survived twenty-eight years without diminishing. Fawful remembers. Fawful always remembers. The defeat in the Beanbean Kingdom wasn't merely a setback; it was a humiliation that Fawful has been processing through the specific lens of someone whose entire self-worth was tied to serving Cackletta competently and who failed to prevent her defeat. That failure created a wound that three decades of empire-building haven't healed. It may have created the MOTIVATION for the empire-building—the need to prove that Fawful is not a failed assistant but a force in his own right, capable of accomplishments that dwarf anything Cackletta imagined.

What Fawful is planning—beyond the occupation, beyond the alliances, beyond the gala announcement—connects to something he calls "the completion" in fragmentary references recovered from Bramblehaven's intelligence cache. The completion is expected before the end of the current month. Its nature is unknown. Its scope, based on the resources Fawful has assembled, is terrifying. Five dragons. Hundreds of soldiers. Peach's Castle. Twenty-eight years of preparation.

Whatever the completion is, it's not simple conquest. Fawful could have conquered territory overtly at any point during his preparation period. He chose not to. He waited. He built. He positioned. And now, with dimensional instability fracturing reality around Raventree Manor and the kingdom's factions tearing each other apart, he's ready to complete whatever he's been building toward since a green mustache helped defeat his mistress in the Beanbean Kingdom twenty-eight years ago.
biography.public: A small Beanish man with enormous round glasses and a grin that contains too many teeth arranged in configurations that shouldn't fit a mouth that size. He hovers in a mechanical pod of his own design and speaks in metaphors that make linguists weep. Everything about him says 'harmless lunatic' except his eyes, which say 'I've been planning this since before you were born.'

description.value:
Fawful's signature mechanical headgear serves as transportation, weapons platform, and personal protection system. The device sits atop his head like a helmet and extends into a hovering pod that allows sustained flight and provides a stable platform for his various weapon systems. The engineering is Beanish in origin—a tradition that prioritizes function over aesthetics and considers exposed wiring a design feature rather than a flaw—but the power source is something Fawful added himself during his twenty-eight years of independent development.

The headgear contains a miniaturized power core that Fawful claims runs on "the mustard of your doom," which—after extensive analysis by multiple intelligence services—appears to mean concentrated fury channeled through alchemical compounds that shouldn't be stable and yet somehow are. The core powers the flight mechanism, the weapons systems, the shields, and the various secondary functions that Fawful has added over decades of continuous modification. The headgear is never the same twice; he improves it constantly, adding capabilities and refining systems with an obsessive attention to detail that suggests the device is as much a part of his identity as the glasses and the grin.

The headgear provides AC 18 (natural armor), flight at 50 feet with hover capability, and serves as the delivery system for Fawful's various attack options. Destroying the headgear (AC 18, 50 HP, immune to psychic and poison damage) grounds Fawful and removes his access to most ranged weaponry, but he remains dangerous even without it—the headgear supplements his capabilities rather than creating them.
description.chat: The headgear hums with energy that shouldn't exist in a device this size, carrying its pilot through the air with the casual defiance of someone who considers physics a suggestion.

unidentified.name: Mechanical Hover Platform
unidentified.description: A complex mechanical device worn as headgear that provides flight and serves as a weapons platform. The engineering is unlike any recognized tradition, and the power source defies standard analysis.

description.value:
The headgear's primary weapon system: a concentrated beam of energy that Fawful fires from apertures mounted on either side of the pod. The beam's color shifts based on Fawful's emotional state—red when angry, green when amused, purple when he's about to do something that will make everyone present wish they'd stayed home. The damage type varies correspondingly: fire when red, acid when green, necrotic when purple. Fawful controls the beam's emotional calibration instinctively, weaponizing his own psychological state with an efficiency that trained magical artificers find both impressive and deeply unsettling.

The beam fires in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 damage on a failure (type depending on emotional state) or half on a success. Fawful can fire the beam twice per round, alternating between apertures, and the rapid-fire capability means enemies who dodge the first beam often move into the path of the second.
description.chat: "I HAVE FURY!" The beam confirms this assessment, delivering concentrated emotional energy in wavelengths that burn, dissolve, or decay depending on which emotion is doing the burning.

unidentified.name: Variable Energy Beam
unidentified.description: A beam weapon that changes damage type based on the wielder's emotional state. The variability makes defensive preparation difficult.

description.value:
The headgear contains a powerful vacuum system that Fawful can activate to inhale objects, projectiles, and even small creatures toward himself. The vacuum creates a 30-foot cone of pulling force that requires each creature in the area to succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be pulled 15 feet toward Fawful. Objects not being held are automatically pulled to Fawful's position. Projectiles fired through the cone have disadvantage on attack rolls as the vacuum disrupts their trajectory.

Fawful uses the vacuum tactically: pulling melee combatants toward his ranged position to create confusion, absorbing thrown weapons and repurposing them, and—in one documented instance—inhaling a cloud of smoke that an enemy was using for concealment and spitting it back as a choking hazard. The vacuum's versatility reflects Fawful's general approach to engineering: build something that does one thing and then find seventy-three additional applications through creativity that borders on mania.
description.chat: The headgear inhales and suddenly everything not nailed down starts moving toward the small man with the enormous grin, including you.

description.value:
During his twenty-eight years of preparation, Fawful obtained and consumed a fragment of the Dark Star—an artifact of catastrophic power that nearly destroyed the Mushroom Kingdom during a crisis that official records have minimized even more aggressively than they minimized the Chaos Heart Crisis. The Dark Star is the counterpart to the Star Rod and the Star Spirits: where they represent hope, wishes, and cosmic benevolence, the Dark Star represents entropy, corruption, and the consumption of light.

Consuming the fragment didn't grant Fawful cosmic power on the scale of the God Toad or even a Star Shard Bearer. What it did was fundamentally alter his physiology, granting him resistances and capabilities that Beanish biology doesn't normally support: resistance to fire, lightning, and cold damage; immunity to charmed and frightened conditions; and the ability to generate the fury energy that powers his headgear from his own body rather than from external fuel sources. He is his own power plant. The dark fragment makes him self-sustaining in ways that conventional technology cannot match.

The fragment also connects him to the broader cosmic architecture that the God Toad's scattered Star Shards represent. The Dark Star fragment is not one of the nine Shards, but it resonates with them—a discordant note in the cosmic music that the Shards collectively produce. Fawful can sense Star Shard activity at distances that suggest cosmic awareness operating through the dark fragment's connection to the star-power spectrum. He knows about the Oracle. He knows about Bryan. He may know about the God Toad's grand design, though his interpretation of that design would reflect the dark fragment's corrupted perspective.
description.chat: Something dark powers him from within, consumed decades ago, integrated so thoroughly that the distinction between Fawful and the fragment has become academic.

description.value: Fawful makes three attacks: two Fury Beam blasts and one of the following: Vacuum Inhale, Fawful Bomb deployment, or Dark Pulse. He typically opens with Vacuum Inhale to disrupt enemy formations, follows with Fury Beams to deal damage to clustered targets, and reserves Dark Pulse for situations where enemies are resistant to his beam weapons.
description.chat: Three attacks from different systems, each one calculated to complement the others in a sequence that looks chaotic and functions with mechanical precision.

description.value:
Small mechanical devices that Fawful deploys from compartments in his headgear, each one shaped like a miniature version of his own face—grinning, bespectacled, and entirely too cheerful for something that explodes. The bombs hover briefly after deployment, tracking toward designated targets with rudimentary guidance systems before detonating in bursts of fury energy.

Each bomb targets a creature within 60 feet. The target must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d8 fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Fawful can deploy up to three bombs as a single action, targeting the same or different creatures. The bombs can be destroyed before detonation (AC 12, 5 HP each), but their small size and erratic flight patterns impose disadvantage on attack rolls made to hit them.

The grinning faces are Fawful's personal aesthetic choice. He considers them intimidating. Everyone else considers them deeply creepy in a way that intimidation doesn't quite capture.
description.chat: Miniature grinning faces hover toward their targets with the cheerful inevitability of something that's about to ruin someone's day.

unidentified.name: Guided Explosive Devices
unidentified.description: Small hovering bombs shaped like faces that track toward targets before detonating. The design aesthetic is deeply unsettling.

description.value:
Fawful channels the Dark Star fragment within him, releasing a pulse of concentrated entropic energy in a 30-foot radius centered on himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 6d10 necrotic damage and has its hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken until it finishes a long rest. On a success, a creature takes half damage and suffers no maximum reduction.

The Dark Pulse is Fawful's most powerful single attack, and he uses it sparingly—the fragment's energy is finite and regenerates slowly, meaning overuse could deplete reserves he needs for the completion. When he does use it, the effect is unmistakable: the area around Fawful dims as light itself is consumed by the pulse, colors bleach to grayscale, and living things feel a moment of absolute despair as the dark energy passes through them.

The pulse also disrupts magical effects in the area. Active spells of 3rd level or lower in the area are automatically dispelled. Higher-level spells require a DC 19 check using Fawful's Intelligence modifier to dispel. This disruption reflects the Dark Star's fundamental nature: it doesn't just damage, it UNMAKES, reducing complex magical constructs to their component energies.
description.chat: Light dies around him. Color bleaches. Hope folds. The dark fragment speaks through Fawful's body and everything within range learns what entropy feels like from the inside.

description.value:
Fawful speaks in elaborately mangled metaphors, food-based analogies, and grammatical constructions that seem to have been assembled by someone who learned language from a book about language that was itself badly translated. "I HAVE FURY!" "Your power is the power of a baby ant who cannot lift even the smallest grain of mustard!" "The taste of your defeat will be like the sourness of a lemon that has married the bitterness of a thousand coffees!"

This is deliberate. The speech patterns are a tactical tool that creates cognitive dissonance in opponents: they can't take him seriously because his words are absurd, but they can't dismiss him because his actions are devastatingly effective. The gap between how Fawful sounds and what Fawful does creates a processing delay that gives him tactical advantage—enemies who are trying to parse his metaphors are not preparing for his attacks.

Creatures who hear Fawful speak for the first time must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be momentarily confused by the dissonance, suffering disadvantage on their first attack roll or ability check against him as their minds struggle to reconcile "food metaphor lunatic" with "extremely dangerous combatant." Creatures who have previously encountered Fawful are immune to this effect, having learned the hard way that the mustard is always metaphorical and the fury is always real.
description.chat: "You are like a sandwich that has forgotten its bread, which is to say you are merely the MEAT and I am the TEETH!" He is already attacking while you try to figure out what that means.

description.value:
Fawful maintains confirmed alliances with five dragons, each one representing military capability that exceeds conventional military formations. The dragons are bound to Fawful through arrangements that intelligence services have been unable to fully characterize—some appear to involve mutual benefit, others suggest leverage or coercion, and at least one appears to involve the kind of genuine respect that powerful beings occasionally develop for minds they consider equals.

In combat encounters, Fawful can use a legendary action (2 actions) to call for dragon support if a dragon ally is within 1 mile. The dragon arrives within 1d4 rounds and acts on its own initiative, following Fawful's general tactical direction without requiring turn-by-turn commands. The dragon alliance transforms any encounter with Fawful from a fight against a single powerful individual into a fight against that individual plus a creature whose breath weapon alone might be sufficient to end the engagement.

The relationship between Fawful and the Dragon Conspiracy—the fabricated war between dragons and the Regal Empire maintained through sonic control devices—is unclear. Fawful may be aware of the conspiracy and exploiting it. He may have allies among the "free" dragons who have escaped sonic control. Or he may be using the conspiracy's infrastructure for his own purposes, piggybacking on Legion technology with modifications the Legion doesn't know about.
description.chat: Five dragons answer when he calls. Five. The number matters because one dragon is a crisis and five dragons is an army.

description.value: Three times per day, when Fawful fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. The Dark Star fragment's energy reinforces his existence against magical effects that would incapacitate or control him. He has survived things that should have killed him—Cackletta's defeat, decades of underground operation, the consumption of a cosmic fragment that should have destroyed his physiology—and simple magical compulsion isn't going to stop someone who has been too stubborn to die for twenty-eight years.
description.chat: The spell fails. Fawful grins. "Your magic is like a sandwich thrown at a WALL. It makes a mess but the wall does not CARE."

description.value:
Fawful can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn.

Reposition (1 action): Fawful moves up to his fly speed without provoking opportunity attacks, repositioning to optimal range for his weapons.

Bomb Drop (1 action): Fawful deploys a single Fawful Bomb at a target within 60 feet.

Dragon Call (2 actions): Fawful signals a dragon ally within 1 mile. The dragon arrives within 1d4 rounds.

Fury Overcharge (3 actions): Fawful overcharges his headgear, firing a supercharged Fury Beam that deals double damage (16d6) in a 60-foot line. After using this ability, the headgear requires 1 round to cool down, during which Fawful cannot use Fury Beam or Fawful Bombs.
description.chat: Between other people's turns, Fawful repositions, deploys, and overcharges, operating at a tempo that conventional combatants cannot match.

description.value:
Fawful remembers the "green mustache." Twenty-eight years have not diminished the grudge against Luigi that was born when the Mario Brothers defeated Cackletta in the Beanbean Kingdom. This grudge is not rational—or rather, it is rational within Fawful's internal logic, where his worth was defined by service to Cackletta and his failure to prevent her defeat invalidated that worth entirely. Luigi represents the moment Fawful became nothing. Everything since—the empire-building, the dragon alliances, the Dark Star fragment, the occupation of Peach's Castle—has been partly motivated by the need to prove that the nothing can become everything.

When Fawful encounters Luigi (or anyone associated with the Mario Brothers), he gains advantage on all attack rolls against that target for 1 round as fury-fueled focus sharpen his capabilities. However, he also has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws for the same duration, as the emotional intensity that enhances his combat performance also makes him more vulnerable to effects that target his clearly compromised judgment regarding anything green-mustache-related.

This vulnerability is exploitable. Anyone who recognizes Fawful's grudge can provoke it deliberately, trading increased danger from his enhanced attacks for the tactical opportunity created by his weakened mental defenses. Making Fawful angry makes him dangerous. Making Fawful angry about Luigi makes him dangerous AND predictable, and predictability in combat is a weakness that skilled opponents know how to exploit.
description.chat: "The green mustache. I REMEMBER the green mustache. I have been remembering for TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS." The fury isn't metaphorical anymore.

description.value:
Fawful is working toward something he calls "the completion," referenced in fragmentary intelligence recovered from Bramblehaven and in overheard conversations at his gala. The completion is expected before the end of the current month. Its nature is unknown to outside observers. Its scope, based on the resources Fawful has assembled—five dragons, hundreds of soldiers, Peach's Castle, the Dark Star fragment, twenty-eight years of preparation—suggests an event of transformative significance.

The completion may involve the dimensional instability at Raventree Manor. The completion may involve the Star Shards and the God Toad's grand design. The completion may involve Peach's secret hatch and whatever evidence it contains. The completion may involve something entirely separate that nobody has anticipated because Fawful has been planning in dimensions that conventional analysis doesn't reach.

Whatever it is, the completion represents the culmination of twenty-eight years of work by the most strategically gifted mind currently operating in the region. It will not be simple. It will not be preventable through conventional means. And it will not be what anyone expects, because Fawful's genius lies precisely in doing things that nobody expects while making everyone believe he's doing something else entirely.
description.chat: "The completion is like a CAKE that has been BAKING for twenty-eight YEARS and now the OVEN is opening and YOU are not READY for how delicious the FURY will TASTE." He means it. All of it. Including the cake part, somehow.

description.value:
Fawful has been preparing for the current moment for twenty-eight years. This preparation manifests as comprehensive contingency planning that covers virtually every scenario. He has agents in every major faction. He has supply caches in locations that other powers don't know exist. He has escape routes from every position he occupies. He has backup plans for his backup plans, each one designed for a specific failure mode that his analysis identified as possible.

Mechanically, Fawful cannot be surprised. He has advantage on saving throws against traps and ambushes. Once per day, when an enemy action would produce a result that Fawful didn't anticipate, the DM may rule that Fawful DID anticipate it—he had a contingency in place, a prepared response, a resource positioned exactly where it needed to be. This reflects not supernatural prescience but the kind of exhaustive strategic preparation that twenty-eight years of obsessive planning produces.

The limitation is that Fawful's preparations are based on his own analysis, which is brilliant but not omniscient. Truly random events—the kind of chaos that the party generates through unpredictable decision-making and the involvement of entities like Waluigi—can exceed his contingency framework. He can plan for competent enemies. He cannot plan for incomprehensible ones.
description.chat: He planned for this. Whatever this is, he planned for it twenty-eight years ago and has been refining the plan ever since. You are not surprising him. You are confirming his expectations.

description.value: Medium Toad. The Feyward variant is a parallel-reality survivor. No ancestry memories are assumed to be shared with Original Dan.
Dan survived Prismari's school, a goblin ambush, the Mazebound, and multiple plane fractures. Suggested proficiencies: Insight, Persuasion, Survival, and Sylvan.

Once per short rest, open the third eye for 1 minute. You can perceive invisible creatures and identify the approximate seam of a nearby portal or planar disguise. The eye is noticeable and may attract attention.

When Dan casts a spell or crosses a planar boundary, the GM may introduce a harmless or dangerous Feyward complication: color inversion, a misplaced door, involuntary apology, or a brief duplicate shadow.

Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement by a cleric or paladin of good alignment)

This platinum amulet is shaped like the sun with a large crystal set in its center. It is sacred to the good-hearted faithful of Barovia and predates any organized church there. Legend says a giant raven (or an angel in raven form) delivered it to the paladin Lugdana, who used it against vampires until her death.

The holy symbol has a number of charges equal to your proficiency bonus + 2 (minimum 3). It regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

While you are attuned to the holy symbol, it functions as a holy symbol for the purpose of spellcasting and channel divinity.

Base Powers (Character Level 3–4)

  • Hold Lesser Vampires (1 charge). As an action, present the holy symbol. Vampire spawn within 15 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier, whichever is higher) or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A paralyzed target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. True vampires are immune to this effect.

  • Empowered Turning (2 charges). When you use Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, you may expend 2 charges. Undead of CR 1 or lower have disadvantage on the saving throw against the effect.

Level 5–8 Improvements

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 3.

  • Hold Lesser Vampires range increases to 20 feet and now also affects vampires of CR 5 or lower (still no effect on Strahd or unique named vampires of higher CR unless the DM rules otherwise).

  • Empowered Turning cost drops to 1 charge and affects undead of CR 2 or lower.

  • Sunlight (3 charges). As an action, present the holy symbol to shed bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. The light is sunlight and lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it (no action required).

Level 9–12 Improvements

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 4.

  • Hold Vampires (1 charge). Range increases to 30 feet. Affects all vampires and vampire spawn (except those the DM designates as legendary or uniquely resistant). Paralyzed duration remains 1 minute with saves at the end of each turn.

  • Empowered Turning now affects undead of CR 3 or lower and costs 1 charge.

  • Sunlight radius increases to 20 feet bright / 20 feet dim and lasts 5 minutes.

Level 13+ (Full Power)

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 5 (capped at 10).

  • Hold Vampires uses the original DC 15 (or your spell save DC if higher) and functions exactly as the classic version.

  • Empowered Turning costs 2 charges and grants disadvantage to all undead against your Turn Undead / Turn the Unholy.

  • Sunlight (4 charges) sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet for up to 10 minutes.

Additional Notes

  • The item never exceeds 10 charges regardless of proficiency bonus.

  • At every stage the light created by the Sunlight property is true sunlight for the purpose of vampire weaknesses and similar effects.

  • The DM can further gate specific powers (especially affecting true vampires or Strahd himself) behind story milestones if desired.

Michael Broussard

Paladins are united by their oaths to stand against the forces of annihilation and corruption. Whether sworn before a god's altar, in a sacred glade before nature spirits, or in a moment of desperation and grief with the dead as the only witnesses, a Paladin's oath is a powerful bond. It is a source of power that turns a devout warrior into a blessed champion.

Paladins train to learn the skills of combat, mastering a variety of weapons and armor. Even so, their martial skills are secondary to the magical power they wield: power to heal the injured, smite their foes, and protect the helpless and those who fight at their side.

Almost by definition, the life of a Paladin is an adventuring life, for every Paladin lives on the front lines of the cosmic struggle against annihilation. Fighters are rare enough among the ranks of a world's armies, but even fewer people can claim the calling of a Paladin. When they do receive the call, these blessed folk turn from their former occupations and take up arms and magic.
